page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor with a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture supports AVX and AVX512F instructions, alongside AES cryptography and FMA. It is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded gzip compression landing in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core execution scales effectively, achieving average tier results in stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory read bandwidth is average at 92.61 GB/sec for large blocks, though the overall PassMark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.sn1ne.8xlarge offers a high density of dedicated physical cores relative to memory, making it a viable option for parallelizable workloads that do not require massive per-core memory allocations. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications such as software compilation, static web serving, and moderate database operations, where parallel processing can offset the lower single-core clock speed. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or memory-intensive databases.
